quote: One cannot think well, love well, sleep well, if one has not dined well.
source: Virginia Woolf, A Room of One’s Own, chapter one, after the dinner at Fernham (Hogarth Press, 1929)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg Australia plain text of A Room of One’s Own, downloaded and searched this run: the sentence wraps lines 541 to 542, between the chapter markers ONE (line 60) and TWO (line 728), in Mary Seton’s sitting room after the Fernham dinner, followed by The lamp in the spine does not light on beef and prunes
evidence.edition: A Room of One’s Own, Hogarth Press, 1929; Woolf’s own English, no translator
evidence.locator: chapter one, after the dinner at Fernham
